summary: Mars Hexalogic Mission Control is a front-end web app whose main job is to simulate and compare the geological and environmental data of Earth with Martian analog soils (like the samples from the Atacama Desert and Antarctica). The project is an integrated dashboard that pulls together weather data from NASA, geographic coordinates, and comparative analytics to support exploratory research.  The app interface is clean and modern, featuring interactive navigation and live data visualizers, along with structured comparison tables that show the differences in planetary properties like soil composition, temperatures, and atmospheric pressure. This system helps researchers or mission managers easily monitor environmental readings, evaluate mission feasibility, and review any telemetry details through a responsive design. In short, the project takes raw scientific data and turns it into a solid, user-friendly web tool for planetary soil research and mission planning.
details: : Mars Hexalogic Mission Control is a front-end web application designed to simulate and compare geological and environmental data between Earth and Martian analog soils, such as samples from the Atacama Desert and Antarctica. It operates as an integrated dashboard that pulls in NASA-derived meteorological data, geographic coordinates, and comparative analytics. The platform empowers researchers and mission operators to seamlessly monitor environmental metrics, assess mission feasibility, and review detailed telemetry, bridging raw scientific datasets with intuitive web technologies for planetary soil research and mission planning. Built using modern web development tools and structured code, featuring responsive design elements, interactive data visualizers, and dynamic comparison tables. The project addresses the challenge of interplanetary exploration by offering a clean, user-friendly interface that translates complex planetary data into actionable insights while ensuring robust performance and responsiveness across devices.
